newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian economic team says "Vision" on course.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian economic team says "Vision" on course.

text.p: The leader of a group of Nigeria's most influential economic figures on Thursday said discussions were making steady progress on a plan to restore wealth to the resource-rich country.

"We have learnt so much since we embarked on this voyage, but there is much more to learn in the weeks and months ahead," Ernest Shonekan, chairman of "Vision 2010" told the 172-member committee in the capital, Abuja.
The second session of the committee, which is to deliver its plan by September, began on Thursday and will end on Saturday.
Among the members are the managing directors of the multinational oil companies working in Nigeria as well as government officials, bankers, businessmen and traditional chiefs.
"During this workshop .. we will break out into different groups where we will actually begin to develop scenarios and visions for the world and Nigeria," Shonekan said.
The committee first met in December to discuss strategies for creating the plan, proposed by military ruler General Sani Abacha, which is modelled on those of Asian nations, notably Malaysia.
Abacha replaced Shonekan, a businessman and advocate of economic deregulation, in a coup during the chaos that followed the annulment of 1993 presidential elections by the military.
Despite producing roughly two million barrels of crude oil every day, Africa's most populous nation of 110 million people remains trapped in poverty and economic stagnation.
